name: Japanese Spiraea
grown_as: A low ornamental shrub, William's is 'Magic Carpet' ('Walbuma'), grown for its coloured leaves: young shoots bright copper-red, maturing to golden yellow. The plain species has green leaves; photos of the species will not show the gold.
habit: A low, dense, spreading mound, 40 to 60 cm high and 60 to 80 cm wide, of many thin, upright, brown twiggy stems.

leaf.outline: Lance-shaped to narrowly oval, small, 2 to 5 cm long
leaf.margin: Sharp, forward-pointing teeth, often double, on the upper two-thirds; the base untoothed
leaf.veins: A midrib and a few side veins running forward
leaf.colour: 'Magic Carpet': copper-red when young, golden yellow when grown, so tips are red over a gold mound; orange-red again in autumn

flower.form: A flat-topped head of many tiny flowers, fluffy with stamens
flower.centre: Many long stamens sticking out well beyond the petals, giving the fuzzy look
flower.carried: In dense flat-topped heads (corymbs) 4 to 8 cm across at the tips of the shoots, held upright above the leaves
flower.size: Each flower 4 to 6 mm; head 4 to 8 cm

fruit: Tiny dry brown pods (follicles) in clusters of five, making a rusty-brown star-studded head that stays on into winter.
seedling: Not drawn: grown as bought plants
winter: A low twiggy mound of thin brown stems, many still topped with flat rusty-brown seed heads; small reddish buds.

leaf: small lance-shaped leaf with sharp teeth on the upper part only
golden yellow, with red on young leaves
bloom: a flat head of many tiny pink five-petalled flowers
long stamens making it look fluffy
young: a low clump of thin upright stems
small pointed leaves, red at the tips, gold below
dormant: a low twiggy mound of thin brown stems
flat brown seed heads left on top
flower: flat pink heads on top of the shoots
a low mound of golden leaves beneath
growing: a low dense mound of golden leaves
copper-red young leaves at the shoot tips

look_alikes: Spiraea 'Goldflame' and 'Goldmound' are close relatives with similar gold leaves. Bridal wreath spiraeas have white flowers in spring along arching stems. Pink yarrow has flat heads too but feathery leaves and is not woody.
